extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduates or graduate students studying algebraic geometry/homological algebra (readers of Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Introductory textbook material defining and giving the basic properties and useful theorems about adjoints, additive and abelian categories, kernels/cokernels, complexes, exactness, and interaction of functors with (co)limits and homology. Aimed at learning how these notions are defined and used in proofs and constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additive category (Ad1–Ad3)
rubrics_metrics.description: A category C is additive if: Ad1. For each A,B in C, Mor(A,B) is an abelian group and composition distributes over addition; Ad2. C has a zero object; Ad3. C has products (hence coproducts) of any two objects (finite products/coproduts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remarks explain that finite products are also finite coproducts in an additive category; additive functors preserve zero objects and products; the abelian group structure on Hom can be constructed from product/coproduct universal properties (φAB). Examples: ModA and category of free A-modules. Use this as the baseline when verifying a category has additive structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernel and cokernel (universal property)
rubrics_metrics.description: Kernel of f:B→C is a map i:A→B universal with respect to f∘i = 0; cokernel is defined dually. The kernel (resp. cokernel) is unique up to unique isomorphism by universal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Kernels are limits and cokernels are colimits. The kernel is a morphism (not just an object). Use the universal diagram to check kernel/cokernel properties. In practice, verify existence by constructing the appropriate subobject/quotient as in module categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abelian category axioms
rubrics_metrics.description: An abelian category is an additive category satisfying: (1) every map has a kernel and cokernel; (2) every monomorphism is the kernel of its cokernel; (3) every epimorphism is the cokernel of its kernel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From these three properties, the usual behavior of kernels, cokernels, images, etc. follows. Image is defined as im(f)=ker(coker f) when it exists. Many arguments can be reduced to ModA via Freyd–Mitchell embedding when comfortable; otherwise check properties by interpreting objects as modules in examples (sheaves, modules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness at a term and definition of short exact sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: A sequence ... → A —f→ B —g→ C → ... is a complex at B if g∘f = 0, and is exact at B if ker g = im f. A short exact sequence is 0 → A → B → C → 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exactness equivalently characterized by kernels/cokernels: exact at B means cokernel of f is a cokernel of ker g, etc. Use these equivalences to convert between diagrammatic and universal-property arguments. Several basic equivalences (e.g., 0→A→0 exact iff A=0) are given as checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology of a complex
rubrics_metrics.description: If ... → A —f→ B —g→ C → ... is a complex at B, the homology at B is H = ker g / im f (more precisely the cokernel of im f → ker g).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complex is exact at B iff its homology at B is 0. Understand cycles as elements of ker g and boundaries as elements of im f. Indexing conventions: decreasing/increasing indexing leads to homology/cohomology notation. Factor long complexes into short exact sequences to analyze homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category of complexes ComC is abelian
rubrics_metrics.description: For an abelian category C, the category ComC (objects are complexes in C, morphisms are degreewise commuting diagrams) is an abelian category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proofs may be done in the special case ModA for intuition. This fact implies that categorical constructions (kernels/cokernels/images/short exact sequences) can be carried out degreewise for complexes; it is used to define homology as a functor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homology functor Hi : ComC → C is covariant
rubrics_metrics.description: Taking homology gives functors Hi from ComC to C; a map of complexes induces maps on homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Show that a morphism of complexes induces maps on kernels/cokernels and hence on homology. Use this to propagate exactness information and to build long exact sequences in homology.

rubrics_metrics.name: Homotopic maps induce the same maps on homology
rubrics_metrics.description: Two maps of complexes f,g : C• → C′• are homotopic if there exist maps w: Ci → C′i+1 with f − g = d w + w d; homotopic maps induce the same map on homology.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the standard fact used to pass to homotopy categories; check by constructing the induced map on cycles and boundaries and showing they coincide on homology classes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Long exact sequence in homology from a short exact sequence of complexes
rubrics_metrics.description: A short exact sequence of complexes 0→A•→B•→C•→0 induces a long exact sequence ... → Hi−1(C•) → Hi(A•) → Hi(B•) → Hi(C•) → Hi+1(A•) → ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires defining the connecting homomorphism Hi−1(C•)→Hi(A•) naturally. In ModA this follows from standard diagram chasing or from spectral sequence arguments; a direct argument or Snake Lemma variant is suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exactness of functors: right-exact, left-exact, exact
rubrics_metrics.description: An additive covariant functor F:A→B is right-exact if A′→A→A′′→0 exact in A implies F(A′)→F(A)→F(A′′)→0 is exact in B. Left-exact is defined dually; exact means both left- and right-exact. Contravariant versions are given similarly (left-exact for contravariant means 0→F(A′′)→F(A)→F(A′) exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these definitions to check preservation of exact sequences under standard functors (localization, Hom, tensor, etc.). Examples/exercises: localization ModA→ModS−1A is exact; ⊗ M is right-exact; Hom(C,·) is left-exact; finitely presented M produces identification S−1 Hom ≅ HomS−1(...).

rubrics_metrics.name: FHHF Theorem (interaction of homology and exactness of functors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Suppose F:A→B is a covariant functor of abelian categories and C• is a complex in A. (a) If F is right-exact, there is a natural morphism F(Hi(C•)) → Hi(F(C•)). (b) If F is left-exact, there is a natural morphism Hi(F(C•)) → F(Hi(C•)). (c) If F is exact, these morphisms are inverses (isomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hints are given: use images/cokernels/ker sequences and functoriality to build the maps. Specialize to tensor with N to see the flatness notion: N is flat iff ⊗N is exact (hence commutes with homology). Use this theorem to deduce when homology commutes with operations like localization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoint functors (definition and units/counits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functors F:A→B and G:B→A are adjoint if for all A in A and B in B there is a natural bijection τAB : MorB(F(A),B) ≅ MorA(A,G(B)). The associated natural transformations η: idA → G F (unit) and ϵ: F G → idB (counit) satisfy the triangle identities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check naturality diagrams for maps f:A→A′ and g:B→B′. Exercises describe constructing ηA and ϵB via τ and its inverse and verifying properties (e.g., Gϵ ∘ ηG = idG, ϵF ∘ Fη = idF). Examples: (⊗A N, HomA(N,·)), (Ind,Res) in representation theory, (π−1, π∗) for sheaves, groupification/forgetful adjoint pairs, localization as left adjoint to forgetful inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjoints interact with (co)limits and exactness
rubrics_metrics.description: If (F,G) is an adjoint pair, then left adjoints commute with colimits and right adjoints commute with limits. Consequently, left adjoints are right-exact (cokernels are colimits) and right adjoints are left-exact (kernels are limits).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to deduce functorial exactness properties: F commutes with colimits ⇒ F is right-exact; G commutes with limits ⇒ G is left-exact. Proposition: right adjoints commute with limits (proof via universal property and adjunction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Filtered colimits are exact in ModA (but not in arbitrary abelian categories)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the category of A-modules, colimits over filtered index categories are exact. However, in general abelian categories filtered colimits need not be exact (Grothendieck's AB5 axiom addresses this).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise to show filtered colimits commute with homology in ModA using FHHF. A counterexample in Ab shows that inverse limits (dually) may fail exactness without extra hypotheses (e.g., limit of Z/p^n gives Z_p and sequence may fail exactness). Be cautious applying filtered-colimit exactness outside module-like categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kernels commute with limits; right adjoints commute with limits
rubrics_metrics.description: If a:i↦Ai and b:i↦Bi are diagrams and h: a→b is a natural transformation with components hi:Ai→Bi, then lim ker hi ≅ ker(lim hi). More generally, right adjoint functors commute with limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This formalizes that limits preserve kernel constructions; use universal properties to prove isomorphisms. Dual statements hold for cokernels/colimits and left adjoints.
